To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reactivation of tabun-, paraoxon- or VX-inhibited hACHE with Ortho-4 and Ortho-5 is not possible.
The reactivation kinetics of bis-pyridinio-aldoximes with human acetylcholineesterases inhibited with different OPs are highly dependent on the linker length and the OP structure.

1) The linker length of bis-pyridin-2-ylmethanols influences the reactivation kinetics of OP-inhibited hACHE, 2) the affinity of the oximes to native enzyme is higher than to OP inhibited enzyme, 3) the reactivation kinetics depends on the OP structure, 4) the reactivation rate constant of tabun inhibited hAChE increases from Ortho-6 to Ortho-8.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new oximes for the treatment of organophosphorous intoxication.
the design and evaluation of new oximes with improved efficacy for the treatment of OP poisoning.
the design of novel oximes that may be more efficient against OP-inhibited hACHE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reactivation of OP-inhibited h AChE is dependent on the structure of OP and the linker length in the bis-ortho-pyriniumaldoxime structure, and that the most effective oximes should be selected on the basis of their affinity to OP-inhibited AChE.
the reactivation kinetics of Ortho-N are strongly dependent on the OP structure, the linker length and the oxime structure.
the linker length is a key determinant for oxime affinity to OP-inhibited hAChe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bis-pyridinumaldoximes are a promising new class of oxime compounds.

the reactivation constants of the tested bis-ortho-polyoximes depend on the OP structure as well as the linker length and that the most promising oximes for reactivating tabuin-inhibited hAchE were Ortho-6, Ortho-7, Ortho-8, and Ortho- 9.
the linker length of a bis-pyridium compound has a strong influence on the affinity and reactivity of the compound to OP-inhibited hACHE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reactivation kinetics of the bis-pyridiumaldoximes is strongly dependent on the structure of the OP.
a higher affinity of the oxime to OP-inhibited hACHE compared to native hACHE is a prerequisite for a successful reactivation.
the oxime linker length plays a key role in reactivating OP-inhibited AChE and that the linker length should be optimized for the particular OP to achieve the best reactivation.
